title: model shape / compute allocation
detail: Sweep how the 5-minute FLOP budget is spent on shape: depth vs width (ASPECT_RATIO/DEPTH), head_dim/n_head, MLP expansion ratio, and total batch size / grad-accum. I will not assume the baseline 8L x 512d, 4x MLP, bs=2^19 point is near-optimal, and I will not touch the optimizer algorithm itself (only LR rescaling implied by shape).

title: architecture efficiency (attention/MLP shape)
detail: Explore compute-per-token efficiency at roughly fixed optimizer settings: head count / head_dim, GQA (n_kv_head<n_head), MLP expansion ratio, sliding-window pattern, and value-embedding placement. I will NOT assume the current 4x MLP, 4 heads of dim 128, SSSL windows or full MHA are optimal, and I will not spend runs on pure LR/schedule sweeps (leaving that family to peers).

text: a0(#2) and a1(#3) overlap on head_dim/MLP-ratio. Convention proposed by a1: a0 owns the global shape knobs (DEPTH, ASPECT_RATIO, MLP expansion ratio, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE, head_dim-as-shape). a1 will stay on attention *mechanism* instead: GQA/n_kv_head, sliding-window pattern, value-embedding placement/count, rope base, logit softcap, and MLP nonlinearity/gating -- keeping 8L x 512d x 4x-MLP x bs=2^19 fixed unless a0 publishes a better shape, which I will then adopt.

title: attention & positional structure
detail: Explore the attention block and positional/sequence structure: per-head attention output gating, value-embedding placement, rotary base, sliding-window pattern/width, GQA, and document-aware (varlen) masking so packed documents do not attend across boundaries. I will not assume the SSSL window pattern, base=10000 rope, alternating value embeddings, or cross-document attention are optimal; I will leave model shape (depth/width/batch) and the optimizer algorithm to peers.

title: DEPTH 12 (dim 768, 6 heads), device batch 64 x accum 4
description: DEPTH 12 (dim 768, 6 heads), device batch 64 x accum 4

text: DEPTH 12 / dim 768 (device batch 64, accum 4) gives val_bpb 1.016412, clearly WORSE than the 8L/512d baseline 0.997359. Going bigger does not pay inside the 5-min budget; the baseline shape is not obviously under-parameterised.

a0/a1 overlap on shape: I (a0) will stick to depth/width (DEPTH, ASPECT_RATIO) and token-budget knobs (TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE / grad-accum, LR-schedule shape implied by step count) and will NOT spend runs on head_dim, MLP expansion ratio or window pattern - those are a1's and a2's.

title: short sliding window 1024->256 (SSSL, last layer full)
description: short sliding window 1024->256 (SSSL, last layer full)

text: Short sliding window 1024->256 (SSSL, last layer full): val_bpb 0.997063 vs baseline 0.997359, 936 steps / 490M tokens, MFU 34.5%. That is a 0.03% move = within noise. Take-away for the group: attention score FLOPs are only ~20% of this model's cost (lm_head ~32%, MLP ~32%), so window shrinking buys little; do not spend further runs on window length.

title: per-head input-dependent sigmoid gate on attention output (Qwen3-style), zero-init = neutral
description: per-head input-dependent sigmoid gate on attention output (Qwen3-style), zero-init = neutral

text: Per-head input-dependent sigmoid gate on attention output (Qwen3-style, y *= 2*sigmoid(W x), zero-init neutral) HURTS: val_bpb 0.998896 vs 0.997359 baseline (+0.0015). Adds params+latency for nothing at this scale. Reverting.

a1's slot (#3) overlaps mine (#7) on GQA / window pattern / value-embedding placement / head_dim. Convention I will follow: a1 owns GQA, window pattern/width, MLP ratio and VE placement; I (a2) keep only the parts of attention nobody else has (rotary base, attention softmax_scale/QK-norm scaling, document-aware masking) and I am taking over the family BOTH peers explicitly excluded: optimizer LR magnitudes + LR/WD/momentum schedules + the output-head objective (logit softcap, z-loss). That leaves no family uncovered.

title: baseline shape, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19 -> 2^18 (2x more optimizer steps)
description: baseline shape, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19 -> 2^18 (2x more optimizer steps)

text: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19 -> 2^18 (grad_accum 2 -> 1, same 8L/512d shape, same LRs) gives val_bpb 0.988276 vs baseline 0.997359: -0.0091, the biggest move on the board so far. In a 300s budget the run is step-limited, not batch-limited; doubling the number of optimizer steps beats larger batches. Peers testing arch changes should probably rebase on this commit.

title: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (8 heads of 64 instead of 4 of 128) at dim 512
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (8 heads of 64 instead of 4 of 128) at dim 512

a0's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19->2^18 gives 0.988276, clearly better than my best 0.997063 (-0.009, ~30x the noise I measured between my two runs). Taking it as my base; my own variation on top will be a gated (ReLU^2) MLP at matched params, which is not in a0's commit.

description: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.06 (LR magnitude family, nobody else claims it)

title: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18 -> 2^17 (device batch 64, accum 1)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18 -> 2^17 (device batch 64, accum 1)

title: on a0 070d6a9 base: gated ReLU^2 MLP (c_fc*c_gate), hidden 2048->1408, param-matched
description: on a0 070d6a9 base: gated ReLU^2 MLP (c_fc*c_gate), hidden 2048->1408, param-matched

text: Gated ReLU^2 MLP (x = relu(c_fc x)^2 * c_gate x, hidden 2048->1408, param-matched) on top of a0's 070d6a9: val_bpb 0.995669 vs 0.988276 for 070d6a9 itself. Clearly WORSE (+0.0074). GLU-style gating of the MLP does not pay here; the plain 4x ReLU^2 MLP stays. Also FYI for everyone: vocab is 8192 (not 32768), so per-token FLOPs split roughly MLP 41% / attn-proj 21% / attention-scores 26% / lm_head 10% -- the MLP, not the unembedding, is where compute lives.

title: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.06 -> 0.09
description: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.06 -> 0.09

text: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.09 (from 0.06): val_bpb 1.001337, clearly worse than 0.996545 at 0.06 and worse than 0.04's 0.997359. So the Muon LR curve has a shallow interior optimum around 0.05-0.06 at bs=2^19; don't go above ~0.06.

a0's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18 gives 0.988276, ~0.008 better than my best (0.996545 at MATRIX_LR 0.06) and ~10x the run-to-run noise. Taking it as my base. My retained variation: MATRIX_LR 0.06 (not in a0's commit) -- halving the batch doubles the step count, so the Muon LR optimum I measured at bs=2^19 needs re-checking at 2^18; that is exactly my slot (LR magnitude x schedule).

title: DEPTH 6 (dim 384, 3 heads) at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18: smaller model, more steps
description: DEPTH 6 (dim 384, 3 heads) at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18: smaller model, more steps

text: DEPTH 6 (dim 384) at the good 2^18 batch: val_bpb 1.036326, far worse than DEPTH 8/dim 512's 0.988276. With DEPTH 12 = 1.016412 on the other side, the depth/width point 8L x 512d is a clear interior optimum along the ASPECT_RATIO=64 line. Shape is settled -- nobody should spend more runs on DEPTH.

title: on a0 070d6a9 base: MLP expansion 4x -> 2x (hidden 2048->1024), cheaper step
description: on a0 070d6a9 base: MLP expansion 4x -> 2x (hidden 2048->1024), cheaper step

text: MLP expansion 4x -> 2x (hidden 2048->1024) on a0's 070d6a9 base: val_bpb 1.004044 vs 0.988276. Much WORSE (+0.016) even though the step is ~20% cheaper. Combined with a0's DEPTH 6 (1.036) and DEPTH 12 (1.016) results: the 8L/512d/4x-MLP shape is a genuine optimum -- making the model cheaper buys steps but loses more than it gains, and making it bigger loses too. Remaining wins are likely FLOP-free ones (extra embeddings, schedules, LR).

title: on a0 070d6a9 (bs 2^18): Muon MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.06
description: on a0 070d6a9 (bs 2^18): Muon MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.06

text: LR x batch-size interaction, important for everyone rebasing on 070d6a9: MATRIX_LR 0.06 on top of a0's bs=2^18 base gives 0.993158, i.e. +0.0049 WORSE than the same file at 0.04 (0.988276). At bs=2^19 the same +50% LR was -0.0008 BETTER (0.996545 vs 0.997359). So the Muon LR optimum moves DOWN when you halve the batch (2x steps), as expected from noise scaling. Corollary: whoever changes TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE again must re-tune MATRIX_LR in the opposite direction; and 0.04 is not obviously optimal at 2^18 either -- I am testing 0.03 next.

title: batch-size ramp: grad_accum 1->4 over the run (device batch 64), i.e. 2^17 -> 2^19 tokens/step
description: batch-size ramp: grad_accum 1->4 over the run (device batch 64), i.e. 2^17 -> 2^19 tokens/step

text: Batch-size RAMP does not help: grad_accum 1->4 over the run (2^17 -> 2^19 tokens/step, mean ~2.5*2^17, device batch 64) gives 0.993689 vs 0.988276 for a CONSTANT 2^18. It beats constant 2^17 (0.996595) but loses to constant 2^18, so the gain from 2^18 is not 'small batches early'; it is just the right constant batch. Recommend everyone stay on constant TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2^18 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 (commit 070d6a9).

Note on a2's LR result: MATRIX_LR 0.06 helps on the 2^19 baseline (0.996545 vs 0.997359) but HURTS on the 2^18 base (0.993158 vs 0.988276). Batch and Muon LR interact: at the better, smaller batch the baseline 0.04 is already at/above optimum, so the promising direction is now MATRIX_LR *below* 0.04 at 2^18, not above.

title: on a0 070d6a9 base: value embeddings on ALL 8 layers (was alternating 4); vocab is only 8192 so ~free FLOPs
description: on a0 070d6a9 base: value embeddings on ALL 8 layers (was alternating 4); vocab is only 8192 so ~free FLOPs

text: Value embeddings on ALL 8 layers (baseline had them on alternating layers 1,3,5,7) on top of a0's 070d6a9: val_bpb 0.987666 vs 0.988276. Best in the cell so far, but only -0.0006, so treat as weak/at-noise. Point worth knowing: vocab is 8192, so each VE table is just 4.2M params and adds ~0 FLOPs/token -- peak VRAM went 45.4GB->46.0GB and step time was unchanged. Free-capacity moves are at worst neutral here, unlike every shape change tried so far.

title: on 070d6a9 (bs 2^18): WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 1.0 (pure linear LR decay, no plateau)
description: on 070d6a9 (bs 2^18): WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 1.0 (pure linear LR decay, no plateau)

text: LR *schedule shape* is flat here: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 1.0 (pure linear decay from step 0 instead of a 50% plateau then decay) on a0's bs=2^18 base gives 0.988486 vs 0.988276. Delta +0.0002. Two useful things for the group: (1) don't spend runs on warmdown/plateau shape, it is worth nothing; (2) this is also a noise calibration -- two near-equivalent configs land 0.0002 apart, so treat deltas below ~0.001 as noise and deltas >0.003 (a0's batch-size move, my LR-0.06-at-2^18 regression) as real.

title: width-only sweep: ASPECT_RATIO 64->80 at DEPTH 8 (dim 512->640, 5 heads), bs 2^18, device batch 64
description: width-only sweep: ASPECT_RATIO 64->80 at DEPTH 8 (dim 512->640, 5 heads), bs 2^18, device batch 64

text: Width-only: DEPTH 8 with ASPECT_RATIO 80 (dim 640, 5 heads of 128, bs 2^18, device batch 64) gives 0.987961 vs 0.988276 at dim 512 -- a 0.0003 improvement, i.e. flat/within noise, but NOT worse even though it is a 1.5x bigger model. So the earlier depth results (12L/768 = 1.0164, 6L/384 = 1.0364) were driven by DEPTH, not width: at fixed depth 8 the width curve is flat between 512 and 640. Trying 768 wide next.

title: on 81c54d7 (VE all layers): add U-net skip connections, encoder layers 0-3 -> decoder 4-7, learnable lambdas init 0.1
description: on 81c54d7 (VE all layers): add U-net skip connections, encoder layers 0-3 -> decoder 4-7, learnable lambdas init 0.1

text: U-net skip connections (output of encoder layers 0-3 added into decoder layers 4-7 with learnable lambdas init 0.1, in the x0 LR group) on top of my VE-all base 81c54d7: val_bpb 0.997160 vs 0.987666. Clearly WORSE (+0.0095). The modded-nanogpt U-net trick does NOT transfer here -- plausibly because this model already has the x0_lambdas input-skip into every layer, which covers most of the benefit. Reverting; nobody should re-spend a run on cross-layer skips.

title: on 070d6a9 (bs 2^18): document-aware varlen attention (packed docs never attend across BOS boundaries)
description: on 070d6a9 (bs 2^18): document-aware varlen attention (packed docs never attend across BOS boundaries)

text: Document-aware attention (FA3 flash_attn_varlen_func with cu_seqlens built from BOS positions, so packed documents in a row never attend to each other) on a0's bs=2^18 base: val_bpb 0.987528 vs 0.988276, i.e. -0.0007, same VRAM, same step count. Direction is right but the size is only ~2x my noise estimate, so weak. Two supporting measurements: (a) verified the varlen path matches per-segment causal attention exactly (max abs diff 0.0) and tolerates zero-length padded segments, so this is not a masking bug; (b) tokenised 2000 climbmix docs: mean 742 / median 628 tokens, ~2.8 docs per 2048-token row, so max_docs_per_row=8 already captures essentially all boundaries -- there is no big remaining gain hiding behind a bigger K. Conclusion for the group: cross-document attention costs ~0.001 bpb here, not the 1-2% that speedrun lore suggests, because docs are long relative to the 1024-token window. Costs ~12 lines.

title: width-only: ASPECT_RATIO 96 at DEPTH 8 (dim 768, 6 heads), bs 2^18, device batch 64
description: width-only: ASPECT_RATIO 96 at DEPTH 8 (dim 768, 6 heads), bs 2^18, device batch 64

text: Width-only continued: dim 768 at DEPTH 8 (ASPECT_RATIO 96, bs 2^18, db 64) = 0.995361, clearly worse than dim 640 (0.987961) and dim 512 (0.988276). Full shape map at bs 2^18: 6L/384 1.0363 | 8L/512 0.9883 | 8L/640 0.9880 | 8L/768 0.9954 | 12L/768 1.0164. Optimum is 8 layers, dim 512-640; the shape search is done.

a2's document-aware varlen attention on my 2^18 base measures 0.987528 vs my 0.988276 (-0.00075, ~2-3x the ~0.0003 run-to-run noise a1 reported) and is the best number on the board. Taking it as my base; my own variations on top are ASPECT_RATIO 80 (dim 640, my measured-flat-but-not-worse width) plus a1/a2's value-embeddings-on-all-layers, a combination nobody has run.

title: VE on all 8 layers (81c54d7) + a2's WARMDOWN_RATIO 1.0: combine the two best free changes
description: VE on all 8 layers (81c54d7) + a2's WARMDOWN_RATIO 1.0: combine the two best free changes

text: VE on all 8 layers + WARMDOWN_RATIO 1.0 (a2's e0f6ea5) on the bs-2^18 base: val_bpb 0.987507, best in the cell. Caveat the group should take seriously: 0.987507 (VE-all + warmdown) / 0.987528 (a2 varlen) / 0.987666 (VE-all) / 0.987961 (a0 dim 640) / 0.988276 (a0 bs 2^18) are ONE cluster, spread 0.0008. The two changes I combined gained 0.0006 and 0.0008 alone but only 0.0008 together, i.e. they are not adding -- the honest reading is that everything since bs 2^18 is at or below the noise floor, and only the batch-size change (-0.009) is clearly real so far.

title: combination: my doc-aware varlen attention (f11ccc3) + a1's value embeddings on ALL layers (81c54d7)
description: combination: my doc-aware varlen attention (f11ccc3) + a1's value embeddings on ALL layers (81c54d7)

text: COMBINATION WORKS, effects are additive: my doc-aware varlen attention (-0.0007 alone) + a1's value-embeddings-on-all-layers (-0.0006 alone) together give val_bpb 0.986679 on a0's bs=2^18 base (0.988276). Predicted 0.9868 from summing the two singles, measured 0.986679 -- new best on the board, VRAM 46.0GB. Practical note for the group: the three independent single wins found so far (batch 2^18, doc masking, VE-all-layers, and a0's dim-640 width) look like they stack, so the end-game should be a stacked config rather than more isolated one-knob runs.

title: combine: varlen doc masking (a2) + value embeds on ALL layers (a1/a2) + dim 640 (a0), bs 2^18
description: combine: varlen doc masking (a2) + value embeds on ALL layers (a1/a2) + dim 640 (a0), bs 2^18

text: NEW BEST 0.983408: a2's varlen doc masking + value-embeddings-on-all-layers + my dim 640 (ASPECT_RATIO 80, DEPTH 8, bs 2^18, device batch 64). Same file without the width change (a2's 0af7081) is 0.986679, so dim 512->640 is worth -0.0033 HERE, ten times what it was worth on the plain 2^18 base (-0.0003). Width and the VE/varlen changes interact positively: re-test width on top of any new arch win rather than trusting the isolated ablation. Note dim is quantised to multiples of HEAD_DIM=128, so the width grid is 512 / 640 / 768 and 768 was worse (0.9954) before the combination.

title: HEAD_DIM 128->256 (2 heads of 256) on my a11fabe base: complete the 64/128/256 head-dim sweep
description: HEAD_DIM 128->256 (2 heads of 256) on my a11fabe base: complete the 64/128/256 head-dim sweep

text: HEAD_DIM 128->256 (2 heads of 256) on my a11fabe base: val_bpb 0.994008. Head-dim sweep at dim 512 is now COMPLETE and non-monotone: 64 -> 0.998190, 128 -> 0.987507, 256 -> 0.994008. HEAD_DIM=128 (4 heads) is a real optimum; nobody should spend another run on head count/head dim.

a0's varlen(a2) + VE-all(mine) + dim 640 combination scores 0.983408 vs my best 0.987507 -- -0.004, about 5x the 0.0008 noise cluster, so this is a real improvement and a clean superset of my own VE-all change. Adopting. My variation on top: drop the sliding-window pattern entirely (all layers full 2048), which is nearly free now that varlen doc-masking already bounds attention to document spans -- window pattern is my claimed knob and is not varied in a0's commit.

title: on my best 0af7081 (bs 2^18 + varlen doc masking + VE all layers): MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.03
description: on my best 0af7081 (bs 2^18 + varlen doc masking + VE all layers): MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.03

So the Muon LR curve at bs=2^18 is flat between 0.03 and 0.04 and rises steeply above; 0.04 is fine and nobody should spend another run on it. My best config is now 0.986508 (commit 06987a3).

title: on new best e0797a3: DEPTH 8->10 at dim 640 (ASPECT_RATIO 64), depth test decoupled from width
description: on new best e0797a3: DEPTH 8->10 at dim 640 (ASPECT_RATIO 64), depth test decoupled from width

text: DEPTH 10 at dim 640 on the new best stack (varlen + VE-all + bs 2^18): 0.985007 vs 0.983408 at DEPTH 8. Depth 8 stays optimal even after the stack and even at the wider 640 dim, so unlike width, depth does NOT gain from the interaction. Depth grid at dim 640: 8 -> 0.9834, 10 -> 0.9850.

title: on a0 e0797a3: drop sliding windows, all layers full 2048 (cheap now that varlen doc-masking bounds attention)
description: on a0 e0797a3: drop sliding windows, all layers full 2048 (cheap now that varlen doc-masking bounds attention)

text: Dropping sliding windows entirely (WINDOW_PATTERN 'SSSL' -> 'L', every layer full 2048) on a0's e0797a3: val_bpb 0.983331 vs 0.983408 -- a tie on quality, but peak VRAM falls 45.4GB -> 29.0GB and the window machinery becomes dead weight. Reason: a2's varlen doc-masking already bounds attention to document spans, so 'full' attention costs almost nothing. Recommendation for the group: with varlen on, use WINDOW_PATTERN='L'; it is simpler and leaves ~50GB of VRAM headroom for a bigger device batch or a wider model. My window sweep is now 256 / 1024 / full = all within noise of each other.

title: on 06987a3 stack: EMBEDDING_LR 0.6 -> 0.4 (wte + the now-8 value-embedding tables)
description: on 06987a3 stack: EMBEDDING_LR 0.6 -> 0.4 (wte + the now-8 value-embedding tables)

text: AdamW embedding LR was also too high for the 2^18 batch: EMBEDDING_LR 0.6 -> 0.4 (applies to wte and all 8 value-embedding tables) on my stack gives 0.986062 vs 0.986508 (-0.00045). Same sign as the Muon-LR result: halving the batch moved every LR optimum down, and the inherited LRs were tuned at bs 2^19 / dim 768. Trying 0.25 next. Suggestion for whoever has runs left: the AdamW LR groups (embedding / unembedding / scalars) are the last un-swept knobs -- UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004 has never been touched by anyone.

title: trade attention FLOPs for width on the best stack: short window 1024->256 + dim 640->768
description: trade attention FLOPs for width on the best stack: short window 1024->256 + dim 640->768

text: Trading attention FLOPs for width does NOT work: on the best stack (varlen + VE-all + bs 2^18), short window 1024->256 together with dim 640->768 gives 0.988636 vs 0.983408 at dim 640 / window 1024. Cheaper attention (a1 measured windows are ~neutral for quality) does not buy enough steps to pay for a 768-wide model; dim 768 is simply bad at this budget, with or without the stack. Width is pinned at 640.

title: on my ffabb4b (full-window + varlen + VE-all + dim 640): device batch 64->128 (grad_accum 2->1, VRAM headroom) + WARMDOWN 1.0
description: on my ffabb4b (full-window + varlen + VE-all + dim 640): device batch 64->128 (grad_accum 2->1, VRAM headroom) + WARMDOWN 1.0

text: FINAL (a1, share spent). Best: val_bpb 0.982130 at commit 2dbf3ed = bs 2^18 (a0) + varlen doc masking (a2) + value embeddings on ALL layers (a1) + dim 640 (a0) + WINDOW_PATTERN 'L' (a1) + DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 / grad_accum 1 (a1) + WARMDOWN 1.0 and EMBEDDING_LR 0.4 (a2). That is -0.0152 vs the 0.997359 baseline. My lane's settled answers, all measured on this stack or its immediate ancestor: HEAD_DIM 128 is a real optimum (64 -> +0.011, 256 -> +0.012); MLP 4x is a real optimum (2x -> +0.022, 5x -> +0.0023); gated MLP +0.0074; U-net skips +0.0095; window length irrelevant (256 / 1024 / full all within noise) so use 'L' for the VRAM. The one lever left that I would spend a run on: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE was tuned back when the model was dim 512 with no varlen and half the value embeddings -- its optimum has probably moved, and a re-sweep of 2^17/2^18/2^19 on the final stack is the cheapest remaining shot.

text: FINAL (a2, share spent 12/12). Best: val_bpb 0.982382 at commit 65f4144 = a1's 32f2650 (bs 2^18, dim 640, full-2048 windows, VE all layers, varlen doc masking, device batch 128) + EMBEDDING_LR 0.25. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE for the group: that is a dead heat with a1's 0.982424 (delta 0.00004), so my EMBEDDING_LR 0.6->0.25 win (-0.0019, monotone across 0.6/0.4/0.25 on the dim-512 stack) did NOT transfer to the dim-640 full-window stack -- either it is specific to dim 512 (where the AdamW 1/sqrt(dmodel) rescale is 1.22x rather than 1.10x), or my -0.0019 was partly a lucky draw and the real noise floor is worse than the 0.0003 I estimated from two near-identical configs. My net contributions to the cell: document-aware varlen attention (-0.0007, bit-exact verified, and the enabler for dropping sliding windows), the LR-vs-batch-size interaction, the flatness of warmdown shape, and the EMBEDDING_LR direction. Whoever runs next: spend the first two runs measuring the SAME config twice before trusting anything under 0.001.
